metadata.accuracy: well-known, publicly reported installations; coordinates approximate to the site
metadata.note: Included for geopolitical orientation. Nothing here is targeting data — locations are rounded and drawn from open reporting.

properties.name: Sevastopol
properties.note: Historic headquarters of the Black Sea Fleet. Much of the fleet has been dispersed east to Novorossiysk under Ukrainian missile and naval drone pressure.

properties.name: Novorossiysk
properties.note: The Black Sea Fleet's fallback base, doubling as Russia's main southern oil export port.

properties.name: Severomorsk
properties.note: Northern Fleet headquarters on the Kola Peninsula, the hinge of Russia's Arctic and North Atlantic posture.

properties.name: Gadzhiyevo
properties.note: Ballistic missile submarine base on the Kola Peninsula.

properties.name: Baltiysk, Kaliningrad
properties.note: Baltic Fleet base in the Kaliningrad exclave, wedged between Poland and Lithuania. The 65 km of Polish–Lithuanian border beside it — the Suwałki gap — is NATO's most-discussed land chokepoint.

properties.name: Tartus
properties.note: Russia's Mediterranean naval facility in Syria; its long-term status became uncertain after the fall of the Assad government in December 2024.

properties.name: Vladivostok
properties.note: Pacific Fleet headquarters.

properties.name: Faslane
properties.note: Home of the UK's ballistic missile submarines, one of two European nuclear deterrent forces.

properties.name: Rota
properties.note: Spanish base hosting forward-deployed US destroyers for Mediterranean and Atlantic missile defence.

properties.name: Ramstein
properties.note: The hub of US air operations in Europe and the venue that gave its name to the Ukraine Defense Contact Group.

properties.name: Rzeszów–Jasionka
properties.note: The Polish airport near the Ukrainian border that became the main logistics gateway for Western aid into Ukraine.

properties.name: Incirlik
properties.note: Turkish air base long associated with forward-deployed US nuclear weapons.

properties.name: Ørland
properties.note: Norway's main fighter base, covering the northern approaches.

properties.name: Ämari
properties.note: Estonian base used for the rotational Baltic Air Policing mission.

properties.name: Šiauliai
properties.note: The original Baltic Air Policing base in Lithuania.

properties.name: Mihail Kogălniceanu
properties.note: Romanian base on the Black Sea, expanding into one of NATO's largest installations in Europe.

properties.name: Engels-2
properties.note: Strategic bomber base on the Volga, struck repeatedly by long-range Ukrainian drones.

properties.name: Olenya
properties.note: Arctic bomber dispersal base on the Kola Peninsula.

properties.name: Belaya
properties.note: Bomber base near Irkutsk, over 4,000 km from Ukraine and still reached by drone attack in 2025.

properties.name: Hmeimim
properties.note: Russian air base in Syria; its future has been in question since December 2024.

properties.name: Plesetsk cosmodrome
properties.note: Northern launch complex used for ICBM testing as well as military space launches.

properties.name: Sevmash, Severodvinsk
properties.note: The yard that builds Russia's nuclear submarines, on the White Sea.

properties.name: Novaya Zemlya test site
properties.note: The Arctic archipelago used for Soviet nuclear testing, maintained in a state of readiness.

properties.name: Zaporizhzhia NPP
properties.note: Europe's largest nuclear plant, under Russian control since March 2022 with all reactors shut down.

properties.name: Chornobyl
properties.note: The exclusion zone was occupied in the opening weeks of the 2022 invasion; the New Safe Confinement over reactor 4 was damaged by a drone strike in February 2025.

properties.name: Redzikowo Aegis Ashore
properties.note: The Polish half of NATO's ballistic missile defence in Europe, declared operational in 2024.

properties.name: Deveselu Aegis Ashore
properties.note: The Romanian site, operational since 2016 and a standing Russian grievance.

properties.name: Pituffik Space Base
properties.note: Formerly Thule, in north-west Greenland. The northernmost US installation and a node in missile early warning.

properties.name: Fylingdales
properties.note: UK early-warning radar covering the northern approaches.

properties.name: Armavir radar
properties.note: Voronezh-DM early-warning radar covering Russia's southern approaches.
